items.Büchen: Buch takes -er with an umlaut: Bücher.
items.Büchers: The plural of Buch has no -s.

items.Brüdern: Brüdern is the Dativ plural. The Nominativ plural is Brüder.

items.Haus: Haus is the singular. The plural is Häuser.
items.Hause: Hause is an old Dativ form.

items.Ferienen: Ferien is already a plural and takes no further ending.

items.Nachbar: An n-noun takes -n in the Dativ: dem Nachbarn.

items.Kollege: An n-noun takes -n in the Genitiv: des Kollegen.

items.Herr: Herr is an n-noun and takes -n in the Akkusativ: den Herrn.

items.Name: Name is an n-noun and takes -n in the Akkusativ: den Namen.
items.Names: Names is the Genitiv ending. The Akkusativ is Namen.

items.Held: Held is an n-noun: den Helden.

items.Lehrerins: Nouns on -in double the n: Lehrerinnen.
items.Lehrerine: Nouns on -in double the n and end in -en.

items.Museums: Museums is the singular Genitiv. The Latin -um becomes -en: Museen.

items.Kost: Kost means food. The cost of a trip is Kosten, a plural noun.

items.Apfelbaume: Baum takes an umlaut in the plural: Bäume.
items.Äpfelbäume: Only the last part changes: Apfelbäume.

items.Namen: Namen is the plural. The Genitiv singular is Namens.
items.Name: Name needs the Genitiv ending -ns here: des Namens.

items.Thema: Thema is the singular. The plural is Themen.
items.Themas: Themas is not standard. The plural is Themen.

items.Datums: Datums is the Genitiv singular. The plural is Daten.

items.Praktikant: Nouns on -ant are n-nouns: den Praktikanten.

items.Herz: The Genitiv needs an ending. Herz is irregular: des Herzens.

items.Gedanke: Gedanke is an n-noun: den Gedanken.
